feature.text: So, playing it safe is not the safest option with Jesus.

lines.text: When we sing on Sunday mornings, here's what it means: the glory of God that I see in the face of Jesus by the Spirit And the joy and satisfaction and delight that I experience as I behold the glory of Christ is so great, so intense, so deep, so majestic, so profound, that merely talking about it is not sufficient.
Worship is our right response to the glory of God seen in Jesus Christ through the Holy Spirit.
We do not sing as a means of entering into God's presence. We sing as an expression of joy that by the death of Jesus, we are already in God's presence.

I am not saying that worship is only authentic when your emotions are burning white-hot for God. Sometimes, being the fickle, distracted creatures we are, all we have to bring to God is the desire to feel white-hot affection for him again.

We no longer have to fear eternal separation from God. Death for us is a doorway to unimaginable joy. Our sin is conquered. Hell is defeated. Jesus saved us for unending pleasures in his presence forever.

Authentic worship expressed by authentic singing begins with simply asking our Father in heaven to increase our capacity to contain more of the Spirit, and he promises to do that in response to our prayers, right?

external.text: I have no use for cranks who who despise music because it is a gift of God. Music drives away the devil. It makes people happy. They forget thereby all wrath, unchastity, arrogance, and the like. Next after theology, I give music the highest place and greatest honor. I would not exchange what little I know of music for something great. Experience proves that next to the Word of God, Only music deserves to be extolled as the mistress and governess of the feeling of the human heart. We know that to the devil music is distasteful and insufferable. My heart bubbles up and overflows in response to music, which so often refreshed me and delivered me from dire plagues.
external.author: Martin Luther

sermons.title: Living In Light of the Master's Return

lines.text: The servants didn't manufacture the increase. They did work. They did expend energy and try their best, but the master is the one who gives the growth.
Bad theology led to fear, and fear led to a hole in the ground.
So don't dismiss sloth as a harmless weakness. Jesus wants us to see the seriousness of a life that claims him as master, but shows little desire to serve him.
So, playing it safe is not the safest option with Jesus.
The master doesn't simply say, well done. He says, enter into the joy of the Lord. Your master. He invites his faithful servants to share in his own joy.
My desire for you is not simply that you would be busy for Christ, but instead that you would live a life of sustainable fruitfulness for him.

lines.text: Not everything that looks holy produces holiness.
In Christ, there is nowhere further to go. There is nothing higher. There is nothing deeper. There is nothing beyond him. There is nothing superior.
You cannot discipline yourself into union with Christ.
Rules can restrain behavior, but they cannot create spiritual life.
We don't become more mature by drifting away from Christ. We don't become more mature by drifting away from Christ's Church in pursuit of some spiritual insight or secret.
The question that Paul asks, and I'm encouraging all of us to ask, is, does any of it actually bring us closer to Christ?
